description: 8 debugging tasks — spot the off-by-one, the empty-input crash, the mutable default, the injection, the missing null-guard, and produce the correct fix. This is the repair skill ikbi depends on.

questions.question:
This loop reads one past the end of the array. Fix the off-by-one and output ONLY the corrected for-loop header line, nothing else:
for (let i = 0; i <= arr.length; i++) {

def add_item(item, lst=[]):
    lst.append(item)
    return lst
add_item('a')
result = add_item('b')
Given Python's mutable-default-argument behavior, what is len(result)? Answer with ONLY the number.

What class of security vulnerability is in this code, and why?
query = "SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = '" + userName + "'"

A buggy leap-year check is: function isLeap(y){ return y % 4 === 0; }
For how many of these four years does the CORRECT leap-year rule (divisible by 4, except centuries not divisible by 400) disagree with the buggy one? Years: 1900, 2000, 2100, 2024. Answer with ONLY the number.

This throws when user or user.profile is missing: const name = user.profile.name;
Make it null-safe. Output ONLY the corrected right-hand-side expression (the part after the '='), nothing else.

metadata.author: luak-coding-suite
metadata.diagnostic_purpose: Tests the repair skills ikbi relies on: finding off-by-one errors, empty-input crashes, Python mutable-default bugs, SQL injection, and missing null-guards — and producing the correct fix. Mixes output-prediction (verified) with bug-identification and corrected-line checks.

known_scoring_limitations: Free-text bug explanations are scored on key concept phrases; an unusually-worded but correct answer could be marked wrong.
